evidence: config.py:521 `bedrock_model_id: str = DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID`
config.py:633-639 reads it from `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` into the field
A repo-wide search for `bedrock_model_id` returns only its definition (config.py:521) and env read (config.py:633) — no consumer anywhere in src/
The invoked model string comes from `_pai_model(cfg)` which reads only `cfg.model`: anthropic_model.py:150 `m = cfg.model` ... :157 `return f"{prefix}:{m}"` — it never references `bedrock_model_id`
By contrast `bedrock_region_name` IS consumed (bedrock_model.py:67 `region = cfg.bedrock_region_name or None`), making the missing wiring of `bedrock_model_id` an inconsistency rather than intent

The live test and ticket AC both select the model via `cfg.model`/`REBAR_LLM_MODEL=bedrock:<id>`, not via `bedrock_model_id`: tests/external/test_bedrock_cache_live.py `model=f"bedrock:{DEFAULT_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID}"`
advisory.finding: The new `bedrock_model_id` config field / `REBAR_LLM_BEDROCK_MODEL_ID` env var is dead configuration: it is defined, env-read, and documented, but no code path consumes it, so setting it has no effect on which Bedrock model is invoked.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runner-level test: with a model resolving to `supports_temperature=False` and cfg.temperature=0, assert `model_settings` carries no `temperature` key (reuse `_capture_model_settings`).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:399-408 `if not caps.supports_temperature: ... else: model_settings["temperature"] = float(temperature)`
search of tests for `supports_temperature` returns only capabilities-level assertions (tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:65-159), never a runner run
An established spy harness for exactly this exists: tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py:47 `_capture_model_settings` captures the Agent's `model_settings`.
advisory.finding: The new runner behavior that OMITS `temperature` from `model_settings` when `caps.supports_temperature` is False is untested end-to-end. Only `caps.supports_temperature` (the input fact) is asserted at the capabilities layer; no test drives `PydanticAIRunner.run()` for a temperature-fatal model and asserts the temperature key is absent from the Agent's model_settings.
scenarios: A refactor inverts or drops the `not caps.supports_temperature` guard: temperature=0 is again sent to us.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7, Bedrock 400s on every Pass-2 gate run, and no unit test fails.
advisory.suggested_fix: Extend tests/unit/test_llm_temperature.py's spy harness with a case whose caps report supports_temperature=False and assert `'temperature' not in ms`.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a runner-level test: `FunctionModel` raising a 400 'temperature is deprecated for this model' makes `run()` raise `LLMConfigError` naming the model, and an unrelated 400 still raises `LLMUnavailableError`.
evidence: src/rebar/llm/runner.py:523-532 `sampling_err = translate_sampling_parameter_rejection(exc, ran_model); if sampling_err is not None: ... raise sampling_err from exc`
search of tests for `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` returns only direct-helper calls (tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:213,232,260) — never through the runner
An existing seam already injects a ModelHTTPError through run(): tests/unit/test_llm_failure_classifier.py:212 `def _raise_429(...): raise ModelHTTPError(429, ...)` driven via `FunctionModel`.
advisory.finding: The runner's sampling-parameter-rejection wiring is untested: `runner.run()` now tries `translate_sampling_parameter_rejection` FIRST in its broad except and re-raises `LLMConfigError` (naming the model) instead of the previous `LLMUnavailableError`. Only the standalone translator is unit-tested; no test drives a model that raises a temperature-deprecation error through `run()` and asserts the surfaced type is `LLMConfigError`, nor that an unrelated 400 still surfaces as `LLMUnavailableError`.
scenarios: A refactor mis-orders the translation after the LLMUnavailableError classification, or drops the try-first call: a temperature-deprecation on an unlisted model reverts to an opaque LLMUnavailableError (the exact misclassification this story exists to prevent) and every test still passes.
advisory.suggested_fix: Mirror `test_runner_attaches_llm_outcome_at_the_generic_seam`: inject a ModelHTTPError(400, 'temperature ... deprecated ...') via FunctionModel and assert `pytest.raises(LLMConfigError)`, plus a contrast case asserting `LLMUnavailableError` for a non-sampling 400.
